classification.difficultyReason: Students must choose to compare 600 with the mean and SD. They find that 600 is exactly 1 SD below the mean, then use the 16% tail to judge a real-world guarantee. The numbers are cleaner than in the reference and the verdict is less subtle, but the demand is similar: an unsignposted interpretation of the empirical rule.

content.prompt:
A drink manufacturer guarantees that each bottle contains at least 600 mL.
The bottles have mean 603 mL and standard deviation 3 mL. Is the guarantee realistic? Why?

answer.short: No: 600 mL is $1$ standard deviation below the mean, so about $16\%$ of bottles would contain less than 600 mL.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}z&=\frac{600-603}{3}\\z&=-1\end{align*}$$
Approximately 68% of bottles lie within one standard deviation of the mean, so the two tails share 32%.
$$\text{Percentage below }600\text{ mL}=\frac{100\%-68\%}{2}=16\%$$
About 1 bottle in 6 would fall short of the guarantee, so it is not realistic.
